title.en: Participle Clauses (Walking home, … Having finished, … Exhausted by the trip, …)
title.es: Las cláusulas de participio (Walking home, … Having finished, … Exhausted by the trip, …)

text.en: A participle clause shortens a whole clause: instead of “While I was walking home, I met a friend” you say “Walking home, I met a friend.” It has three main forms: the -ing form (simultaneous or a reason), having + participle (an earlier action), and the past participle (a passive meaning): “Exhausted by the trip, he fell asleep.” The Spanish gerundio (“Caminando por la calle…”) matches it, but in English the subject of the participle must always be the subject of the main clause.
text.es: Una cláusula de participio acorta una cláusula completa: en lugar de «While I was walking home, I met a friend» se dice «Walking home, I met a friend.» Tiene tres formas principales: la forma -ing (simultánea o una razón), having + participio (una acción anterior) y el participio pasado (sentido pasivo): «Exhausted by the trip, he fell asleep.» El gerundio del español («Caminando por la calle…») le corresponde, pero en inglés el sujeto del participio debe ser siempre el sujeto de la oración principal.

title.en: The -ing form: simultaneous action or a reason
title.es: La forma -ing: acción simultánea o razón

text.en: The -ing form replaces “while” or “because”. Both actions have the same subject: “Feeling tired, she went to bed early.”
text.es: La forma -ing reemplaza a «while» o «because». Las dos acciones tienen el mismo sujeto: «Feeling tired, she went to bed early.»

examples.es: Walking down the street, I met an old friend.

tr.en: Walking down the street, I met an old friend.
tr.es: Caminando por la calle, me encontré a un viejo amigo.

examples.es: Feeling tired, she went to bed early.

tr.en: Feeling tired, she went to bed early.
tr.es: Sintiéndose cansada, se fue a dormir temprano.

text.en: If the first action comes before the second, having + participle is used. Negative: not having + participle. Passive: having been + participle.
text.es: Si la primera acción ocurre antes de la segunda, se usa having + participio. Negación: not having + participio. Pasiva: having been + participio.

examples.es: Having finished the report, he went home.

tr.en: Having finished the report, he went home.
tr.es: Habiendo terminado el reporte, se fue a casa.

examples.es: Having been told the news, she began to cry.

tr.en: Having been told the news, she began to cry.
tr.es: Al enterarse de la noticia, empezó a llorar.

title.en: The past participle: a passive meaning

text.en: The past participle gives the meaning “because something was done to it”: “Written in simple English, the book is easy to read.” “Frightened by the noise, the baby cried.”
text.es: El participio pasado da el sentido «porque algo se le hizo»: «Written in simple English, the book is easy to read.» «Frightened by the noise, the baby cried.»

examples.es: Written in simple English, the book is easy to read.

tr.en: Written in simple English, the book is easy to read.
tr.es: Escrito en inglés sencillo, el libro es fácil de leer.

examples.es: Frightened by the noise, the baby started to cry.

tr.en: Frightened by the noise, the baby started to cry.
tr.es: Asustado por el ruido, el bebé empezó a llorar.

title.en: Negative, conjunction and the subject rule
title.es: Negación, conjunción y la regla del sujeto

text.en: The negative is not before the participle: “Not knowing the way, we asked a stranger.” With a conjunction: after leaving, while waiting, on arriving, before going. The subject of the participle is the subject of the main clause: “Walking down the street, I saw an accident.”
text.es: La negación es not antes del participio: «Not knowing the way, we asked a stranger.» Con una conjunción: after leaving, while waiting, on arriving, before going. El sujeto del participio es el sujeto de la oración principal: «Walking down the street, I saw an accident.»

examples.es: Not knowing the way, we asked a stranger.

tr.en: Not knowing the way, we asked a stranger.
tr.es: Sin saber el camino, le preguntamos a un desconocido.

examples.es: After leaving school, she worked in a bank.

tr.en: After leaving school, she worked in a bank.
tr.es: Después de salir de la escuela, trabajó en un banco.

text.en: The subject of a participle clause is normally the subject of the main clause: “Walking down the street, I saw an accident” (I was walking). If the main clause has a different subject, a separate clause must be used. Fixed exceptions: judging by, generally speaking, considering, given, weather permitting.
text.es: El sujeto de una cláusula de participio es normalmente el sujeto de la oración principal: «Walking down the street, I saw an accident» (yo caminaba). Si la oración principal tiene otro sujeto, hay que usar una cláusula aparte. Excepciones fijas: judging by, generally speaking, considering, given, weather permitting.

text.en: Spanish influence: the Spanish “sin saber” can be not knowing in English; it does not have to be “without knowing”. The Spanish “al llegar” is on arriving, and “por ser médica” is being a doctor.
text.es: Influencia del español: el «sin saber» del español puede ser not knowing en inglés; no tiene que ser «without knowing». El «al llegar» es on arriving, y «por ser médica» es being a doctor.

speak.en: A participle clause shortens a whole clause: «Walking down the street, I met an old friend». The -ing form expresses a simultaneous action or a reason: «Feeling tired, she went to bed early». «Having» plus the participle marks an earlier action: «Having finished the report, he went home». The past participle has a passive meaning: «Written in simple English, the book is easy to read». In the negative «not» comes before the participle: «Not knowing the way, we asked a stranger». The subject of the participle is the subject of the main clause.
speak.es: Una cláusula de participio acorta una cláusula completa: «Walking down the street, I met an old friend». La forma -ing expresa una acción simultánea o una razón: «Feeling tired, she went to bed early». «Having» más participio marca una acción anterior: «Having finished the report, he went home». El participio pasado tiene sentido pasivo: «Written in simple English, the book is easy to read». En negativo «not» va antes del participio: «Not knowing the way, we asked a stranger». El sujeto del participio es el sujeto de la oración principal.

gloss.en: a bad event, often with cars
a person you do not know

items.sentence: ___ down the street, I met an old friend.

why.en: A simultaneous action, the same subject: Walking down the street, I…
why.es: Una acción simultánea, el mismo sujeto: Walking down the street, I…

Walked.en: “Walked down the street, I” is not correct; you need the -ing form.
Walked.es: «Walked down the street, I» no es correcto; hace falta la forma -ing.

To walk.en: “To walk down” would express a purpose, not a simultaneous action.
To walk.es: «To walk down» expresaría una finalidad, no una acción simultánea.

examples: Driving home, I heard the news.

tr.en: Walking down the street, I met an old friend.
tr.es: Caminando por la calle, me encontré con un viejo amigo.

items.sentence: ___ tired, she went to bed early.

why.en: A reason, the same subject: Feeling tired, she went…
why.es: Una razón, el mismo sujeto: Feeling tired, she went…

Felt.en: “Felt tired, she” is not a correct participle clause; you need the -ing form.
Felt.es: «Felt tired, she» no es una cláusula de participio correcta; hace falta la forma -ing.

Feel.en: “Feel tired, she” is not correct; you need the -ing form.
Feel.es: «Feel tired, she» no es correcto; hace falta la forma -ing.

tr.en: Feeling tired, she went to bed early.
tr.es: Sintiéndose cansada, se fue a la cama temprano.

items.sentence: ___ finished the report, he went home.

Have.en: “Have finished the report, he” is not correct; you need the -ing form (Having).
Have.es: «Have finished the report, he» no es correcto; hace falta la forma -ing (Having).

Had.en: “Had finished the report, he” is not a correct participle clause; you need Having.
Had.es: «Had finished the report, he» no es una cláusula de participio correcta; hace falta Having.

tr.en: Having finished the report, he went home.
tr.es: Habiendo terminado el informe, se fue a casa.

items.sentence: ___ the way, we asked a stranger.

why.en: The negative: not comes before the participle.
why.es: La negación: not va antes del participio.

Knowing not.en: “Knowing not the way” is old-fashioned; today you say Not knowing.
Knowing not.es: «Knowing not the way» es anticuado; hoy se dice Not knowing.

Not known.en: “Not known the way” is not correct; know here needs the active -ing form (knowing).
Not known.es: «Not known the way» no es correcto; know aquí necesita la forma -ing activa (knowing).

examples: Not wanting to wait, he left.
Not having a key, she knocked.

tr.en: Not knowing the way, we asked a stranger.
tr.es: Al no conocer el camino, le preguntamos a un extraño.

items.sentence: ___ in simple English, the book is easy to read.

why.en: A passive meaning: the past participle, Written.
why.es: Un sentido pasivo: el participio pasado, Written.

Writing.en: “Writing” would mean the book writes; here you need a passive.
Writing.es: «Writing» significaría que el libro escribe; aquí hace falta una pasiva.

Wrote.en: Wrote is the simple past, not a participle; you need Written.
Wrote.es: Wrote es el pasado simple, no un participio; hace falta Written.

examples: Built in a day, it fell.

tr.en: Written in simple English, the book is easy to read.
tr.es: Escrito en inglés sencillo, el libro es fácil de leer.

items.sentence: ___ by the noise, the baby started to cry.

why.en: A passive meaning: Frightened by the noise.
why.es: Un sentido pasivo: Frightened by the noise.

Frightening.en: “Frightening” would mean the baby frightens; here you need a passive.
Frightening.es: «Frightening» significaría que el bebé asusta; aquí hace falta una pasiva.

Frighten.en: Frighten is the base verb, not a participle clause; you need Frightened.
Frighten.es: Frighten es el verbo base, no una cláusula de participio; hace falta Frightened.

examples: Shocked by the news, he sat.
Tired by the trip, she slept.

tr.en: Frightened by the noise, the baby started to cry.
tr.es: Asustado por el ruido, el bebé comenzó a llorar.

items.sentence: After ___ school, she worked in a bank.

leave.en: “After leave” is not correct; after after you need -ing.
leave.es: «After leave» no es correcto; después de after hace falta -ing.

left.en: “After left school” is not correct; after after you need -ing or a subject + verb.
left.es: «After left school» no es correcto; después de after hace falta -ing o sujeto + verbo.

tr.en: After leaving school, she worked in a bank.
tr.es: Después de salir de la escuela, trabajó en un banco.

items.sentence: While ___ for the bus, I read the news.

waited.en: “While waited” is not correct; after while you need -ing.
waited.es: «While waited» no es correcto; después de while hace falta -ing.

wait.en: “While wait” is not correct; after while you need -ing.
wait.es: «While wait» no es correcto; después de while hace falta -ing.

tr.en: While waiting for the bus, I read the news.
tr.es: Mientras esperaba el camión, leí las noticias.

items.sentence: On ___ home, he found the door open.

why.en: On + -ing means: as soon as he arrived.

arrive.en: “On arrive” is not correct; after on you need -ing.
arrive.es: «On arrive» no es correcto; después de on hace falta -ing.

arrived.en: “On arrived” is not correct; after on you need -ing.
arrived.es: «On arrived» no es correcto; después de on hace falta -ing.

tr.en: On arriving home, he found the door open.
tr.es: Al llegar a casa, encontró la puerta abierta.

items.sentence: ___ a doctor, she knows how to help.

why.en: A reason: Being a doctor, she knows…
why.es: Una razón: Being a doctor, she knows…

Been.en: “Been a doctor, she” is not correct; you need the -ing form (Being).
Been.es: «Been a doctor, she» no es correcto; hace falta la forma -ing (Being).

Be.en: “Be a doctor, she” sounds like an imperative; you need the -ing form (Being).
Be.es: «Be a doctor, she» suena a imperativo; hace falta la forma -ing (Being).

tr.en: Being a doctor, she knows how to help.
tr.es: Siendo doctora, ella sabe cómo ayudar.

items.sentence: Walking down the street, ___ saw an accident.

why.en: The participle’s subject is the main subject: the one who walked is the one who saw.
why.es: El sujeto del participio es el sujeto principal: quien caminaba es quien vio.

a car.en: The car did not walk; the subject of the participle would not match.
a car.es: El carro no caminaba; el sujeto del participio no coincidiría.

the accident.en: The accident did not walk; the subject of the participle would not match.
the accident.es: El accidente no caminaba; el sujeto del participio no coincidiría.

tr.en: Walking down the street, I saw an accident.
tr.es: Caminando por la calle, vi un accidente.

items.sentence: ___ having eaten all day, he was very hungry.

No.en: “No having eaten” is not correct; the negative is not.
No.es: «No having eaten» no es correcto; la negación es not.

Don't.en: “Don’t having eaten” is not correct; the negative is not.
Don't.es: «Don’t having eaten» no es correcto; la negación es not.

examples: Not having a car, he walked.

tr.en: Not having eaten all day, he was very hungry.
tr.es: Al no haber comido en todo el día, tenía mucha hambre.

items.sentence: Having ___ told the news, she began to cry.

why.en: A passive, an earlier action: Having been told.
why.es: Una pasiva, una acción anterior: Having been told.

be.en: “Having be told” is not correct; after having you need a participle (been).
be.es: «Having be told» no es correcto; después de having hace falta un participio (been).

being.en: “Having being told” is not correct; after having you need a participle (been).
being.es: «Having being told» no es correcto; después de having hace falta un participio (been).

tr.en: Having been told the news, she began to cry.
tr.es: Habiendo recibido la noticia, ella comenzó a llorar.

items.sentence: ___ by the trip, he fell asleep at once.

why.en: A passive meaning: Exhausted by the trip.
why.es: Un sentido pasivo: Exhausted by the trip.

Exhausting.en: “Exhausting” would mean he tires others; you need a passive.
Exhausting.es: «Exhausting» significaría que él cansa a otros; hace falta una pasiva.

Exhaust.en: Exhaust is the base verb; in a participle clause you need Exhausted.
Exhaust.es: Exhaust es el verbo base; en una cláusula de participio hace falta Exhausted.

tr.en: Exhausted by the trip, he fell asleep at once.
tr.es: Agotado por el viaje, se quedó dormido de inmediato.

items.sentence: Not ___ what to say, she kept quiet.

known.en: “Not known what to say” is not correct; know here needs the active -ing form (knowing).
known.es: «Not known what to say» no es correcto; know aquí necesita la forma -ing activa (knowing).

know.en: “Not know what to say” is not a correct participle clause; you need the -ing form.
know.es: «Not know what to say» no es una cláusula de participio correcta; hace falta la forma -ing.

examples: Not wanting to wait, he left.

tr.en: Not knowing what to say, she kept quiet.
tr.es: Sin saber qué decir, se quedó callada.

items.sentence: Having lost his keys, ___ had to climb in through the window.

why.en: The participle’s subject is the main subject: the one who lost them is the one who climbed in.
why.es: El sujeto del participio es el sujeto principal: quien las perdió es quien trepó.

the keys.en: The keys did not lose anything; the subject of the participle would not match.
the keys.es: Las llaves no perdieron nada; el sujeto del participio no coincidiría.

the window.en: The window did not lose anything; the subject of the participle would not match.
the window.es: La ventana no perdió nada; el sujeto del participio no coincidiría.

tr.en: Having lost his keys, he had to climb in through the window.
tr.es: Habiendo perdido sus llaves, tuvo que entrar por la ventana.

items.sentence: Judging by the sky, it ___ rain soon.

why.en: After “judging by” the main clause gives the expected future: it will rain.
why.es: Después de «judging by» la oración principal da el futuro esperado: it will rain.

is.en: “It is rain” is not correct; the base verb rain asks for a modal.
is.es: «It is rain» no es correcto; el verbo base rain pide un modal.

does.en: “It does rain soon” is not a correct prediction; you need will.
does.es: «It does rain soon» no es una predicción correcta; hace falta will.

examples: Judging by his face, he is ill.
Judging by the news, it will end.

tr.en: Judging by the sky, it will rain soon.
tr.es: Juzgando por el cielo, lloverá pronto.

tr.es: Caminando por la calle, me encontré a un amigo.

text.en: a new subject in the main clause
text.es: un sujeto nuevo en la oración principal

wrong.en: The subject of the participle clause is the same as the main clause (I).
wrong.es: El sujeto de la cláusula de participio es el mismo que el de la principal (I).

text.es: una cláusula acortada: while I was walking, con el mismo sujeto

text.es: una finalidad: caminé para

wrong.es: La forma -ing aquí marca simultaneidad, no una finalidad.

wrong.es: Having + participio marca una acción anterior, no simultánea.
